P01.note: 'attacks a single bacterial species' defines selective directly; toxic is the only near-miss.

P02.note: 'carry the allele' is the standard collocation; the other three are lexically off.

P03.note: Reduce is killed by 'trying to prevent this movement'; tolerate needs the colon clause.

P04.note: Court accepts a reading it would not choose = deference; endorsement is a near-miss but implies agreement.

P05.note: Hesitant is killed by 'states plainly'; hedged fits the bounded scope but is a slightly imperfect fit for a plain claim.

P06.note: Critics who knew the dispute read the omission as deliberate; mysterious is the near-miss for uninformed readers.

P07.note: Left hand as a second voice = layered; nimble is countered by identical tempos/ornaments.

P08.note: Frictional unemployment; imbalance is killed by 'not of a shortage of jobs', inertia is a near-miss.

P09.note: 'far more than speed' alone gives patience.

P10.note: 'earlier, broader ___ give way to the narrower one' about meaning = sense; others are off-axis.

P11.note: Day length triggers restlessness = cue; constraint and challenge are plausible-sounding but wrong.

P12.note: 'Standing in the eyes of others' = face; 'whatever their rank' undercuts hierarchy, harmony is a near-miss.

P13.note: 'accept in exchange for' signals tradeoff within the blank's sentence.

P14.note: Suspend is killed by 'does not shut programs down'; reduced-frequency examples define ration.

P15.note: Clusters sometimes precede quakes but usually fade, so ambiguous; baseless is too strong given the concession.

P17.note: Same diagnoses from a third the scans = higher yield per scan; requires combining the counts.

P18.note: Checking donations for infection = screen; sample is a near-miss from 'small portions'.

P19.note: First circulated version later rewritten = draft; others clearly off.

P20.note: 'won more often' is a modest advantage, so edge over dominance; requires calibrating degree.

P21.note: Expanding the shorthand back including discarded sounds = restore; mostly the blank's sentence.

P22.note: Sound arrives a fraction of a second late = lag; pause is the near-miss.

P23.note: 'would otherwise have moved away' = held (retained); employed is the near-miss undercut by 'less for the jobs it saved'.

P24.note: Few endings, unstable word order = skeletal; rigid is killed by 'word order shifts'.

P25.note: Limits praise to city scenes without retracting = qualifies; 'rather than retracting' frames it.

P26.note: Missing/jumbled bands make the count approximate; arbitrary is too strong.

P27.note: Announced purpose barely pursued = pretext; needs the whole passage but options are distant.

P28.note: Gain vs loss = mass balance; connection/correlation are weaker fits.

P29.note: Performers expected to add their own ornaments = latitude; others off-axis.

P30.note: Pre-release counts needed to measure later decline = baseline; calibration is a near-miss.

P31.note: 'merely ... not what the fish gain' = accompanies; benefits killed by 'survive just as well'.

P32.note: Fins do the cooling instead of machinery = perform; distractors clearly wrong.

P33.note: Seamless exterior hides two separate structures = masks; joins is a near-miss but contradicted by 'covers only the outer frame'.

P34.note: Erase killed by 'keeps every retiree's view'; dampen fits reduced weight.

P35.note: Concealed in house/barn = harbored; fed and ferried ('pointed out the road', 'assisted along the way') planted against.

P36.note: Real to trained players but unnoticed by most = minute; jarring contradicted by unnoticed change.

P37.note: Thickness balanced between strength and oxygen = compromises; 'between protection and breathing' nearly gives it.

P38.note: 'did not simply compete ... it also ___' contrast gives aided.

P39.note: Smaller fraction with more owners = dilutes; devalues killed by 'even where total value rises'.

P40.note: Protection against one class alone = bounded; abiding killed by 'could erase it'.
